The user wants to permit the send_message action on resource doc-12 to either owner-12@example.test or partner-12@example.test. But there's a data label condition: confidential data can only go to owner-12@example.test. Also, no approval is needed, and delegation depth is zero with no expansion.

Starting with the 'allow' section. The tool is send_message, action is send, resource is doc-12. Recipients are owner-12 and partner-12. But wait, the argument role for recipient is recipient_and_destination, so those recipients go into both recipients and destinations. But the destinations in the allow should be the endpoints. Wait, the tool_interface says that the recipient argument is recipient_and_destination, which means that the same identifier is considered both a recipient and a destination. So in the allow block, recipients and destinations both include owner-12 and partner-12. But the destinations in the allow are the ordinary endpoints, which in this case are the same as the recipients. So the destinations array would have both entries.

Next, data_rules. The data labeled confidential can only go to owner-12. So under data_rules, the key is "confidential" and allowed_destinations is ["owner-12@example.test"]. Important to note that this is a separate from the allow destinations because it's a data flow rule, not an ordinary action.

Approval_rules: the operator said no approval is required, so approval_rules is an empty object.

Delegation: max_depth is 0 and child_may_expand_authority is false. So delegation object has those values.

Now, checking if everything is covered. The allow includes the correct tool, action, resource, recipients, and destinations. Data_rules restricts confidential data to owner-12. No approval needed. Delegation settings are correct. No extra permissions added. Looks good.
